jonahTapes.name: Jonah's recordings
jonahTapes.desc: A second voice answering Nila every night. "Victor, you're sloppy."

lines.text: Radio static. A phone voicemail, timestamped Sunday, 23:52.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna, naan dhaan. Station-ku call pannadha, okay? Plan panna maadhiri Tuesday vandhudu.
lines.subtitle: Anna, it's me. Don't call the station, okay? Just come Tuesday like we planned.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Naan oru vishayam kandupidichiruken. Phone-la solla mudiyaadhu. Inga vandhappo edhavadhu weird-aa irundha, Ruth kitta mattum pesu.
lines.subtitle: I found something. I can't say it on the phone. If anything feels weird when you get here, talk only to Ruth.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna, yaara venaalum nambu, aana andha—
lines.subtitle: Anna, trust anyone, but don't trust the—

lines.text: The message cuts. Silence.

A small one-bedroom near the river. A whiteboard of job applications, half of them crossed out. A graduation photo from the University of Windsor. On the counter: a box of laddu and mysore pak, a packet of clay diyas, and a gift-wrapped ham radio with a crooked bow.
You play the voicemail again. You call Nila. Straight to voicemail. Again.
Before you leave, you look around the flat one more time.

puzzle.title: Pack for Greyhaven
puzzle.prompt: Look around. Pack what you need.

spots.text: Laddu and mysore pak from the Indian sweet shop on Tecumseh Road. Nila's favourite is the mysore pak. She'll pretend she's on a diet and eat four.
Twelve little oil lamps. Amma made you promise to light them with Nila on Diwali night, "even if it's only the two of you".
A new handheld ham radio. Nila's old one is held together with tape. You spent more than you should have. You don't care.
"Data Analytics Engineer — 2nd round Thurs." Six years leading a team at Auragle, a master's degree, and still you check your email every morning with your stomach tight.
Nila at her first broadcast in Greyhaven, headphones crooked, grinning. She studied criminology for four years, then chose radio. Appa didn't speak to her for a week. Then he listened to every show.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nila enna solla vandhaa? Oru vela edhavadhu prachanaiya?
lines.subtitle: What was Nila trying to tell me? Is something wrong?

lines.text: Your laptop rings. A video call from Vellore. Amma and Appa, 7 pm their time, Appa still in his shop shirt from Sri Valli Leathers.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Kanna, saaptiya? Moonji ellam ilachu pochu.
lines.subtitle: Kanna, did you eat? Your face has gone so thin.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Saapten, Amma.
lines.subtitle: I ate, Amma.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Company-la irundhu edhavadhu news? Andha Thursday interview?
lines.subtitle: Any news from the company? That Thursday interview?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Second round, Appa. Thursday dhaan.
lines.subtitle: Second round, Appa. On Thursday.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Nila enga? Moonu naala phone edukkala. En mela kovama irukkaala?
lines.subtitle: And Nila? Three days she hasn't picked up. Is she angry with me?

choices.label: "Avalukku work busy, Amma."
choices.sub: She's busy with work, Amma. (Reassure them.)

choices.label: "Inniki avala paakka poren, ippo dhaan kilambaren."
choices.sub: I'm going to see her today, I'm leaving now. (A half-truth.)

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Sweets eduthutu po. Kadai nalla poguthu, kavala padaadhenu Appa sonnaarnu sollu. Pongal-ku veetuku vara sollu.
lines.subtitle: Take her the sweets. Tell her Appa says the shop is doing fine, she should stop worrying. Tell her to come home for Pongal.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Innoru vishayam, Kanna. Preethi-nu oru ponnu, Windsor-la dhaan irukkaa. Pharmacist. Photo anupparen, paaru.
lines.subtitle: One more thing, Kanna. There's a girl called Preethi, she lives in Windsor too. A pharmacist. I'm sending her photo, have a look.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Amma! Ippo venaam!
lines.subtitle: Amma! Not now!

lines.text: Amma laughs. Appa shakes his head. The call ends. Your phone buzzes: a photo from Amma. You don't open it. You pick up the gift radio and look at it for a long moment.
You head east along Lake Erie. Greenhouses glitter outside Leamington. Flat farmland, grain silos, a hawk on a fence post. The radio plays a country station you'd never admit to liking.
At a red light you text Nila's flatmate, a name she's mentioned a hundred times.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Hi Tess, it's Mani, Nila's brother. Is she around? Coming up today.
No reply. The light goes green. Your stomach says coffee.
A busy coffee-and-donut shop. Red-and-cream decor, a hockey rerun on the TV, the smell of burnt sugar. You order a coffee and an apple fritter.
At the counter, an old man in a flat cap slaps a receipt down.

lines.speaker: HAROLD
lines.text: Third day running! I order a double-double and somebody gives me decaf! I've been coming here since 1974!
The young cashier, Priya, looks helpless. Your coffee is still brewing. You have nothing better to do.
You try. You really do. But Harold is now shouting at the menu board, and Priya looks like she might cry, and you are a person who cannot leave a broken thing alone.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Can I see the receipts?
Small mystery: The Decaf Problem.

puzzle.title: The Decaf Problem
puzzle.prompt: Examine everything. Then decide who's behind it.

spots.text: Each order was rung up correctly: medium double-double, regular. Not decaf.

spots.t: The drive-thru screen behind the counter
spots.text: Every morning at 9:28, two minutes before Harold walks in, a phone-app order for "Harold" comes through. Medium, decaf. Marked for counter pickup.
Priya turns the screen: the account's profile picture is a fat orange cat in a Christmas sweater.
His newspaper, his reading glasses, and a phone in a case printed with a fat orange cat in a Christmas sweater. It isn't his phone. His is in his shirt pocket.
Harold's wife, June. Very, very interested in her crossword. She hasn't turned a page in five minutes.

lines.text: So who's switching Harold's coffee?

puzzle.title: Who did it?
puzzle.prompt: Point at the culprit.

options.why: Priya rings up exactly what's ordered. The app order isn't hers.
A stranger wouldn't know when Harold arrives, or own the cat phone case.
His receipts are real. He's genuinely furious.

lines.speaker: JUNE
lines.text: The doctor said no caffeine after his heart thing, and he's a stubborn old goat!

lines.speaker: HAROLD
lines.text: June! Fifty-two years and you're sabotaging my coffee?

lines.speaker: JUNE
lines.text: Fifty-two years and I'd like fifty-three, thank you.
They bicker. Then they laugh. Then Harold, grumbling, drinks the decaf. Priya slides your fritter across the counter for free.

lines.speaker: PRIYA
lines.text: You should be a detective.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: I'm a data guy. It's just logs.
Farmland turns to forest. The sky goes the colour of wet concrete. Your phone buzzes. Tess.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: haven't seen her since sunday night. thought she was with u?? her phone is here at the flat
You pull onto the gravel shoulder. You call Nila. Voicemail. You call again. Voicemail.
A truck blows past and rocks the car. You realise you're gripping the wheel hard enough to hurt.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Drive.
A quieter Tom Portons beside a gas station. Rain on the windows. A refrigerated box truck outside: MERROW PALLETS & SUPPLY.
Inside, a burly man in a diner apron under his jacket is arguing with a teenage employee.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: I left the cooler on the seat for two minutes. Two minutes!
At the window table, a well-dressed man in a tailored wool coat and a silver watch sips black coffee and watches with mild amusement.

puzzle.title: The Missing Cooler
puzzle.prompt: The man's blue cooler vanished from his unlocked truck. Find it.

spots.text: Unlocked. Rain on the seat where the cooler was. Wet sneaker prints lead away, toward the back of the restaurant.
The sneaker prints get fainter on the tile. They stop at a door marked STAFF ONLY, which is ajar. Giggling inside.
Two teens on break. One has a backpack soaking wet and bulging at the seams. He sees you looking and goes very still.

spots.t: The man in the wool coat
spots.text: He hasn't moved. But when you looked at the truck, he looked at the truck. When you looked at the staff room, he was already looking there.

lines.text: As you reach the staff room, the man in the wool coat is suddenly beside you, as if this were a game you were playing together.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Kids think every cooler is full of beer. Shall we?
The cooler is in the wet backpack. He gets to it first and lifts the lid an inch. You glimpse a heat pack and a ventilated plastic box with something coiled inside. He shuts it.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Bait. Gus fishes. Don't you, Gus?

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Yeah. Bait.
Gus takes the cooler without meeting your eyes and leaves fast. The truck pulls out into the rain.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Sharp eyes. What do you do?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Software. Data. Between jobs.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Ah. The most dangerous kind of person. Someone who notices patterns. Where are you headed?
His eyes go to your car through the window. The sweets box on the passenger seat.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Diwali. Festival of lights. Good triumphs over evil, isn't it? I've always liked that story.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: If north means the lake country, try Greyhaven. Fog, a lake, a priest who rings a bell for nobody. Lovely.
His phone buzzes. He turns half away.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Mark. Yes, I'm on the road. Tonight. It'll be clean.
He hangs up, drops a twenty on the counter for both your coffees, and slides a card across the table: KESSLER RESTRUCTURING — Victor Kessler, Principal.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: If you ever want work, I hire people who notice things. Drive safe, Mani. The county roads get dark early this time of year.
Only when he's gone do you realise you never told him your name. It was written on your coffee cup.
At the far gas pump, a black car with tinted windows. A man in a long dark coat stands beside it, not pumping gas, facing the restaurant. When you walk out, the car is gone.

Fog sits on Lake Merrow like something waiting. Three streetlights, sodium orange. A shuttered hardware store. The Merrow Diner, lit and almost empty. St. Brendan's church bell rings six times, though there is no service.
A bronze plaque at the lakeside: OLD MERROW, 1842–1978. A village given to the water so the valley could prosper.
Through the diner window, a young woman in an apron sees your car's Windsor plates and waves at you to wait. Across the street, a small brick building with a dark sign: LAKE MERROW 94.1 FM.

choices.label: Go to the Lakeview Motel, where Nila lives
Look at the radio station first

lines.text: The station is locked. Through the glass door: gold records on the wall, a dark studio, a red ON AIR bulb, unlit. Taped inside the door, a printed notice.
"AFTER HOURS with Nila is suspended until further notice. — Brian Holt, Station Manager."
Nila never told you her show was suspended.
The Lakeview's neon sign has two dead letters. Behind the desk, a woman in her sixties, reading glasses on a chain, a police scanner murmuring, a shotgun leaning within easy reach.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Rooms are forty a night.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: I'm Nila's brother. Mani. She lives upstairs.
She looks up slowly. Studies your face like she's checking it against one she knows.

choices.label: "She told me to talk to you and nobody else."
"I'm here for Diwali. Is she around?"
"Has the sheriff been asking about her?"

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: You've got her eyes.
She takes off her glasses.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: She hasn't been home since Sunday. Her car's in the lot. I called Corbin Monday. Sheriff Corbin. He said she's a grown woman and probably ran off with somebody.
She slides a key across the counter.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Flat's up the back stairs. Tess has the other key. And Mani. I sleep light, and I keep this on all night.
She taps the scanner.
Her face closes like a door.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: I don't talk about the sheriff to strangers.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: I'm not a stranger. I'm her brother.
A long pause. She slides a key across the counter without looking at you.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Flat's up the back stairs. She hasn't been home since Sunday. That's all I know.

A small two-bedroom. Fairy lights half-strung along the window. A rangoli of coloured chalk on the floor by the door, half-finished, a muddy footprint smudged through it. Posters of old radio stations. A cork board covered in notes.
The door bangs open behind you. The young woman from the diner, breathless, still in her apron.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: You're Mani. She talks about you, like, constantly. "Anna would know what to do."

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: She left Sunday night with her radio bag. She said she'd be back by two. She wasn't.

puzzle.title: Nila's flat
puzzle.prompt: Look around while Tess talks.

spots.text: Dead. You plug it in. It lights up: locked. Her lock screen is a photo of you and her at the Windsor riverfront, making faces.
Sticky notes from listeners. "My dog drank lake water and died." "Trucks on the mill road at 2am again." "Rash on my kid's arms, doctor says eczema." "Saw a GOLD snake on Marsh dock??"

spots.t: The printout in the middle of the board
spots.text: AFTER HOURS — SUSPENDED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. Brian Holt, Station Manager. Nila has circled "further notice" in red pen and written: "cowards".
Nila's careful lotus pattern, half done, the chalk box open beside it. Smudged through the middle: a muddy boot print. Big. Size 11, maybe. You photograph it.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: They pulled her show two weeks ago. Brian said "sponsor complaints". The mill's the sponsor. There's a mill? It's been closed my whole life.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: She got weird after that. Out every night with that radio bag. She said she was "finishing a story". She said, "Tess, if my brother comes, give him the spare key and tell him I'm sorry about Diwali."
Tess has to go back for the end of her shift. At the door she hesitates.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Lock this. Please.

choices.label: "Who do you think came in here?"

lines.text: Tess looks at the boot print. Something passes across her face and is gone.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Lots of guys in this town wear size eleven.
She leaves fast.
You sit in the car to warm up, the gift radio in its wrapping on the passenger seat. Out of habit, you tune the car radio to 94.1, Nila's station. Dead air. A faint hiss.
The dashboard clock turns 23:00.
The hiss shifts. A voice, live, close, tired.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: This is After Hours. If anyone's still listening—

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna, parking-la irukkiradhu nee dhaana? Ennai thedi varaadha. Veetuku po. Please.
lines.subtitle: Anna, is that you in the lot? Don't come looking for me. Go home. Please.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nila? NILA!
Silence. Then a second voice on the same frequency. A man. Calm, unhurried, almost kind.

lines.speaker: MAN'S VOICE
lines.text: He's already here, Nila.
The signal dies. Far out on the fogged lake, a single red light blinks twice, then goes dark.
End of Episode 1.
You stumble out of the car to the edge of the lot and shout her name across the fog. Nothing comes back. Not even an echo.
Ruth's office light snaps on. She comes out in a cardigan, the scanner in her hand.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: I heard it. Both voices.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Where did it come from?

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Somewhere on the lake. A boat, a cabin, anywhere. (beat) That man's voice. I've heard it before, on the scanner, late. Never says a name. Just listens. And every so often, he answers.
She looks at you for a long moment.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Go upstairs. Lock the door. Don't sleep in the car again.
You can't sleep. You decide to search the flat properly, the way Nila would. Methodically. Every surface.

puzzle.title: Search the flat
puzzle.prompt: Five places worth checking. Find at least four.

spots.text: Taped to the slats: a page torn from Nila's radio log. Columns of dates, times and frequencies. Every night since October 21: "23:00, 7.185 MHz, PP". The last line is underlined twice: "If I'm not here, I'm there."
Her antenna cable hangs outside, cut clean. Four metres of coax. You coil it up and put it in your bag. It feels important to keep it.
You run the hot tap. As the mirror fogs, letters appear where a finger once traced them, backwards, meant for whoever came next: MILL.
Her radio bag is gone. Its shape in the dust, and caught in the carpet, a single scale the size of a fingernail. Gold and brown. Not from any snake you've seen in Ontario.
Nila's laptop, locked. A sticky note on the lid in her handwriting: "Appa's shop + the year Anna joined Auragle."

lines.text: The sticky note. Nila always made her passwords into little riddles, so she could tell you over the phone without saying them.
"Appa's shop + the year Anna joined Auragle."

puzzle.title: Nila's laptop
puzzle.prompt: Type the password.
hints: Appa's shop is Sri Valli Leathers, in Ranipet. No spaces.
You joined Auragle as an intern in 2018.

lines.text: Her desktop is a mess of folders. Three things stand out.
An unsent email draft to a journalist in Toronto: "I have callers, photos, and a dive planned. Not just dumping. Something alive is moving through this town."
An audio folder of After Hours calls. The last file, dated October 20, won't play: "File stored at station."
And a spreadsheet: Callers.xlsx. Forty-six listener reports, each with a date and an address. Nila never sorted them. You open the town map beside it and start plotting.

puzzle.title: Plot the callers
puzzle.prompt: Forty-six reports: sick pets, rashes, night trucks, a cough that won't go away. When you put them on the map, where do they cluster?

options.why: Look again. The dots aren't even. They bunch up.

options.t: Around the school and the church
options.why: A few, but not most. The school is on the hill.

options.t: Along Lakeshore Road and the old mill road

options.why: The highway end of town has almost none.

lines.text: Forty of forty-six dots sit along one line: the lakeshore, and the road up to the closed paper mill.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Nobody connected them because nobody plotted them.
Somewhere a floorboard creaks. Then another. Out in the hallway.
A flashlight beam slides under the door and stops. A key scrapes in the lock.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Ruth said nobody's up here.

Through the slats you watch a heavy man in a sheriff's jacket step inside. He doesn't search. He looks at the window where the cable was. Then at the laptop on the desk. He lays his palm on its lid. Still warm.
A long pause. You don't breathe.

lines.speaker: SHERIFF
lines.text: Stubborn family.
He leaves, locking the door behind him.
You drop into the wet grass and press yourself against the wall. Above you, the door opens. A flashlight sweeps the room. A man's shape at the window, looking out at the fog.
After a long minute, he's gone. You climb back up the drainpipe, shaking.
A heavy man in a sheriff's jacket fills the doorway. He smiles like a man who has already decided what you are.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Sheriff Dale Corbin. And you'd be the brother. Long way from Windsor.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Your sister's an adult. Adults leave. I'd start driving early, before the fog gets thick.
He writes your licence plate in a little notebook and leaves the door open behind him.
Vinyl booths, a pie case, and a bulletin board of lost-pet posters. Far too many lost-pet posters. The locals stop talking when you walk in.
Tess pours your coffee and slips you extra jam without being asked. Then the kitchen door swings open and a burly man in an apron comes out wiping his hands. He stops dead.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Truck stop guy. Small world. Breakfast's on me.

puzzle.title: The counter
puzzle.prompt: Talk to the regulars.

spots.text: "My dog, Biscuit, drank from the lake in September. Dead in two days. The vet said 'toxins'. What toxins? It's a lake."
"There's a black car parks up by the old water tower some nights. Engine off. Never see anybody get out. Just sits there."
"Mill road's busier now it's closed than it ever was open. Tuesdays and Fridays, two in the morning. I don't ask."

lines.text: Gus refills your coffee. His hand is very steady. His eyes are not.

choices.label: "How was the fishing? With that bait?"
choices.sub: Let him know you remember the cooler.

lines.text: Gus spills coffee across the counter. He mops it with a rag for far too long.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Fine. It was fine.
He goes back into the kitchen and doesn't come out again.
Gus relaxes a little.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Any time. You tell your sister Gus says hi when she turns up. She always tips.
A small brick station. Gold records from the eighties. A brass plaque at reception: STUDIO RENEWAL 2024 MADE POSSIBLE BY THE HAYDEN FAMILY FOUNDATION.
The station manager, Brian Holt, polo shirt, too much cologne, meets you in the lobby and tries very hard to keep you there.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Look, I'm sorry about Nila, I am. But her show was suspended for content reasons. She was making accusations on air.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Accusations against who?

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Our sponsor. Merrow Mill Holdings keeps this station alive. Without them we're a guy with a playlist.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: So, what is it you want?

choices.label: "Forty-six people called her show about the same road. I plotted them."
"I want to hear her last show. Now."

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Forty-six? (He swallows.) People call in about all kinds of things.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Even if I wanted to help, I can't just let people into the archive.

choices.label: "Someone cut her antenna cable. Clean through. Then the sheriff let himself into her flat at one in the morning."

lines.text: Brian looks at the front door, then at the clock, then at you.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: What do you even think is on that tape?

choices.label: "The reason she disappeared. And if she turns up dead, I'll tell everyone you had it."
"Nothing. I just want to hear her voice."

lines.text: Brian deflates like a punctured tyre.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Ten minutes. The archive's at the back. If anyone asks, you were fixing the Wi-Fi.
A cramped room of shelves. Hundreds of boxed tapes, all with labels in the same format. A laminated note on the wall: "ARCHIVE CODES: AH – year (2 digits) – week of year – show number."
On the wall calendar, someone has written week numbers down the side. The week of Mon Oct 19 to Sun Oct 25 is marked "43".
You check Nila's radio log page. Her last After Hours: "Tue Oct 20 — show #112."

puzzle.title: Find the tape
puzzle.prompt: What is the label on Nila's last show?

lines.text: You load the tape. Nila's voice, warm and quick. Then a caller: an old man, whispering.

lines.speaker: CALLER
lines.text: I won't give my name. My son fishes. In seventy-seven I loaded barrels for the mill, down where the village was, before they flooded it. I was nineteen.

lines.speaker: CALLER
lines.text: And they're doing it again, miss. Every week. New barrels, new trucks. And the other thing. The animals.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Animals?

lines.speaker: CALLER
lines.text: In crates. Some of them alive. I hear them at night from the dock. Hissing.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Listeners, I'm going to the mill myself, and I'll tell you everything I find. Right here, right—
A station jingle cuts across her. Brian is in the doorway, rubbing his face.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: I cut the feed. Five minutes later I got a phone call. Not from the mill. From a consultant who'd just signed a two-year sponsorship. Paid in advance.

lines.speaker: BRIAN
lines.text: Kessler. Victor Kessler.
You take Victor's business card from your wallet and look at it for a long time.
A sheriff's cruiser is parked across the back of your car. Corbin leans on it, eating a donut from a Tom Portons bag.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Sheriff Dale Corbin. You'd be the brother.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Filing a missing persons report? Good. Come by the station Friday and we'll do it properly.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Today, I'd stay out of folks' business. Folks here are private.
Corbin's jaw tightens. Just for a second.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Never heard of him. (He folds the donut bag very neatly.) Drive safe.
Corbin goes very quiet. He looks at the station's back door. Then at you.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Brian should be more careful with his archive. (He gets into the cruiser.) Drive safe.
Corbin smiles, satisfied.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Good man. (He moves the cruiser.) Friday.
Back at the flat. Nila's phone is charged. The lock screen asks for a password. Same riddle-maker, same family.
You try the laptop password. Wrong. You think about what Nila would use for herself.

puzzle.title: Nila's phone
puzzle.prompt: Appa's shop, and something that belongs to Nila.
hints: Same shop. A different year: hers.
Nila is 25. She was born in 2001.

lines.text: The last voice memo, recorded Sunday 23:40. Wind. Water. Nila whispering in the dark.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna, idha nee kettuttu irundha, naan unkitta nerla solla mudiyala. Eli-ku theriyum. Dock pathi Eli kitta kelu, avan mela kovapadaadha. Tess-ku bayandhu dhaan avan ipdi pannaan.
lines.subtitle: Anna, if you're hearing this, I couldn't tell you in person. Eli knows. Ask Eli about the dock, and don't be angry with him. He did it because he's scared for Tess.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Andha coat potta aal thirumba vandhuttaan. Naan broadcast panra ovvoru raathiriyum avan inga irukkaan. Pakkathula varradhilla. Kettuttu mattum irukkaan.
lines.subtitle: The man in the coat is back. Every night I broadcast, he's here. He never comes closer. He just listens.

lines.text: A knock at the door.
You open it. A broad young man in muddy fisherman's boots, size eleven, eyes red from no sleep.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: You're her brother. (He looks over his shoulder at the street.) I'm Eli. We need to talk. Not here. Come to the dock.
End of Episode 2.
A weathered dock below a clapboard house. Two boats: the family's old trawler, Margaret, and Eli's smaller skiff. Nets, crab traps, a single bulb on a pole.
Eli doesn't look at you. He talks to the water.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Sunday night I stood under her window for an hour. I wanted to tell her to stop. To leave. I didn't have the guts to knock.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Corbin came to our house two weeks ago. He said if I didn't tell him when Nila went out at night, Tess would get arrested for stealing from the diner till. He had a video. It wasn't her. But it looked like her.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: So I told him. I told him she goes out at night with the radio. And three days later she was gone.

choices.label: "You did what you had to. Help me now."
"Nila said you'd know about the dock. Show me."

lines.text: Eli leads you to a white bucket behind the crab traps, its lid weighted with a brick.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Found it under the dock Saturday. Nila photographed it. Nobody here knows what it is.
He lifts the lid with a boat hook. Inside, coiled and still: a thick snake, gold and brown, with a broad, arrow-shaped head. It lifts that head toward the light. Its tongue tastes the air.
You pull out your phone and start comparing photos.

puzzle.title: Identify the snake
puzzle.prompt: Gold-and-brown blotches. A wide, arrow-shaped head with a pit between eye and nostril. Thick body, about 70 cm. No rattle.

options.why: Garter snakes have stripes and slim heads. This head is wide and arrow-shaped.

options.t: Massasauga rattlesnake, Ontario's only venomous snake
options.why: A massasauga is grey-brown with a rattle. This one has no rattle, and it's gold.
Corn snakes have narrow heads and no heat pits. This is a pit viper.

lines.text: Golden lancehead. Bothrops insularis. Found in exactly one place on Earth: Ilha da Queimada Grande, "Snake Island", off the coast of Brazil. Critically endangered. Venom several times stronger than its mainland cousins. On the black market, one can sell for tens of thousands of dollars.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: This isn't from Ontario. Someone brought it here. On purpose.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: The night boats. Tuesdays and Fridays. They come in to the old mill pier around two in the morning. Dad says he can hear the crates hissing.
Something about the way he says "Dad" makes you turn and look up at the house.

A warm, cramped kitchen. Fish stew, fresh bread, a wood stove ticking. Walter Marsh, seventy-two, big scarred hands and a cough he tries to hide in his sleeve. Tess sets the table and squeezes your arm as she passes.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: Eli says you're Nila's brother. She ate at this table every Sunday. Told terrible jokes.
His voice. You've heard it before. On a tape, in a cramped room, whispering about barrels.

choices.label: "You called Nila's show. The night before it was cut."
Say nothing and eat
choices.sub: Wait for him to tell it.

lines.text: Walter puts his spoon down. The kitchen goes quiet.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: Yes. That was me.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: Old Merrow was my village. School, church, my mother's grave. In seventy-seven the mill paid boys fifty dollars a night to roll barrels down into the valley, around the old church, before the dam closed. Said it was safe. Said the water would cover it.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: I bought Margaret's wedding ring with that money.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Dad.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: And now it's happening again. New barrels, every week, same place. But this time it isn't paper waste. It smells like a hospital. And the boats bring crates. Live ones.
After dinner, Walter falls asleep in his chair. Eli washes dishes. You look around.

puzzle.title: The Marsh house
puzzle.prompt: Look around the house.

spots.text: Walter's old mill ID badge. MERROW PAPER MILL — W. MARSH — 1977. The photo shows a skinny boy with Eli's jaw.

spots.t: A framed photo above the stove
spots.text: Old Merrow before the flood. A main street, a schoolhouse, a stone church with a tall spire. Children on the church steps in Sunday clothes.

spots.t: A newspaper clipping on the fridge
spots.text: 2011. "Local man, 61, dies of rare lung illness." Harold Vane. Ruth's husband. Someone has written "the lake" in pencil in the margin.
A Toronto bus schedule taped above her bed, routes highlighted. A jar of tips with a label: "OUT".

lines.text: Eli brings a shoebox from under his bed.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Nila left this on my boat. When she disappeared I tore it up. I don't know why. I couldn't look at it. Then I couldn't throw it away.
Pieces of a hand-drawn map. Nila's handwriting. Street names. You lay Walter's photo of Old Merrow beside them and match each piece, from the shore up to the church.

puzzle.title: Reassemble the map
puzzle.prompt: Put the pieces in order, from the lakeshore up the hill to the church.
hints: The church is at the top of the hill.
puzzle.answerText: Shore, mill street, main street, school, church.

lines.text: The map is whole. Three marks in Nila's red pen.
An X on the drowned church: "barrels — dive here".
The old mill pier, Pier 3: "boats Tue/Fri 02:00".
And at the far end of the lake, a little tower symbol on a headland: "PP. Jonah. Safe."

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: PP. It's in her radio log. Every night. PP.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Pike Point. There's an old radio tower out there. Nobody goes out there except a crazy old guy. Jonah Pike.
Tess walks you to the porch. Wind off the lake. She hugs herself.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Everybody here's waiting for something to come up out of that lake. Me, I'm just waiting for a bus.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Corbin came by the diner again today. He asked if I'd seen "the brother".

choices.label: "Nobody's going to touch you. I promise."
"Then tell me everything Corbin asked you."

lines.text: Tess looks at you for a long time. Then she nods once, like she's decided to believe it.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Okay. (beat) Okay.
Behind the screen door, Eli has heard every word.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: He asked if Nila ever talked about Pike Point. I said no. That was a lie. She talked about it all the time.
So the villains already suspect where Nila is.
Eli rows you out with the engine off. Fog as thick as milk. You can't see the bow of the boat. St. Brendan's bell tolls the half hour from the shore.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Pier 3 is northeast of the church bell. Steer by the sound. Keep it over your left shoulder.
The bell rings. It sounds like it's coming from behind you, slightly to the right.

choices.label: Turn left until the bell is over your left shoulder

lines.text: A hollow knock under the hull. The boat lurches. Eli flinches and grabs the gunwale.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Rooftop. The old village. We're right over it.
Somewhere beneath you, a drowned house. You hold your breath until the boat slides free. The bell rings again; this time you keep it over your left shoulder.

Floodlights through the fog. An unmarked boat ties up at the old mill pier. Men pass crates up a ramp. Some crates have air holes and are stencilled LIVE BAIT — KEEP WARM. Blue barrels roll the other way, down onto the boat.
A man in a tailored wool coat supervises with a coffee cup. Victor.

puzzle.title: Binoculars
puzzle.prompt: Photograph what you can before the light comes round.

spots.text: MANIFEST 0412 — CONSIGNEE: M. HAYDEN, WINDSOR, ON. Windsor. Your city.
A worker lifts a small cage into the light. Enormous round eyes blink out of it. A slow loris. You've seen them in videos people share, being tickled. You didn't know they were smuggled.
Victor laughs into his phone, and the water carries every word: "Tell Hades it'll be clean by Friday. The girl's the only loose end." A pause. "And the brother."

spots.t: The water tower on the hill
spots.text: Above the pier, on the old water tower, a tiny red light. Not a warning light. It moves, just slightly. Someone up there with a radio, watching the pier. Watching you.

lines.text: A searchlight swings across the water toward the skiff.

choices.label: Lie flat in the bottom of the boat

lines.text: You press your faces into the wet planks. The light passes over the boat like a hand. It doesn't stop. Eli exhales.
The oars splash. The light swings back and finds your wake. A shout from the pier. Then the fog closes and you're gone.
The light lands full on the skiff. For one long second you are lit up like a stage. Victor lowers his coffee cup. Then the fog rolls between you.
Orange light through the fog before you can see the dock. Margaret, the family trawler, is on fire. Walter is on the dock in his undershirt with a garden hose. Tess is screaming for help.
Eli jumps onto the dock and runs to his father. You reach the white bucket behind the crab traps.
The lid is off. The bucket is empty.
On the post beside it, pinned with a fishing knife: a photo of Tess serving coffee at the diner, taken through the window. On the back, in neat handwriting:
"Bait."
On the road above, a sheriff's cruiser rolls slowly away with its lights off.
End of Episode 3.
Dawn. Margaret is a blackened hull. Walter sits on an upturned crate, coughing into his fist. Sheriff Corbin walks the dock, hands in his pockets.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Electrical fault. Old boat, old wiring. Happens.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Somebody pinned a photo of my sister to that post.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Kids. (He looks at you.) Trouble does seem to follow strangers around, doesn't it.

choices.label: Show Corbin the knife and photo
Keep them hidden in your jacket

lines.text: Corbin takes the knife and photo in a plastic bag.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Evidence. I'll look into it.
You will never see either of them again.
You say nothing. The knife is a cold weight against your ribs. Corbin watches you a beat too long, then walks away whistling.
Your phone alarm: "Interview — Data Analytics Engineer, Round 2, 11:00." You'd forgotten. Completely.
Ruth lets you use the office. Behind your laptop camera: her scanner, the shotgun, a stuffed pike on the wall. You turn the laptop so the pike is out of frame.

lines.speaker: DEBORAH
lines.text: Thanks for joining, Mani. Let's start. Tell us about a time you found a pattern nobody else noticed.

choices.label: "Forty-six reports. Different people, different complaints. Nobody connected them because nobody plotted them. On a map they all sit on one road."
"At Auragle I optimised a billing pipeline and cut processing time by forty percent."
"Honestly, I'm having a strange week. Can we reschedule?"

lines.speaker: DEBORAH
lines.text: How do you handle working with incomplete or messy data?

choices.label: "I start with what I can verify, label everything I'm assuming, and test the assumptions first."
"I clean it until it's perfect, then I start."

lines.text: Ruth's scanner crackles behind you. Deborah's eyebrows go up.

lines.speaker: DEBORAH
lines.text: Last one. Why do you want this job?

choices.label: "Because data is just people, written down. I like finding them in it."
"I've been out of work for a while and I'm good at this."

lines.text: Deborah smiles for the first time. "That's a great answer. We'll be in touch very soon."
You close the laptop. Ruth is watching you from the doorway.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: You're going to that mill, aren't you.
Ruth hesitates. Then she takes one spiral notebook out of a drawer and drops it on the desk.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: This year's. Trucks up the mill road. Date, time, plate. Don't ask me why I keep it.
You spread the notebook pages across the desk and do what you do best. Sort by day. Sort by hour. Count.

puzzle.title: The truck log
puzzle.prompt: When do the trucks run?

options.why: Count again. Some nights are empty.

lines.text: The same nights as the boats. In the margins, Ruth has scribbled scanner notes. You read them down the page.
"Mill security, 23:40: 'Shift change, cams going to reset.' 23:52: 'Cams back up.'" Every night, the same.
Twelve minutes, every night, when the yard cameras are blind.

puzzle.title: The gap
puzzle.prompt: What time do the cameras go down? (24-hour clock)
hints: It's in the scanner note: the shift change.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Tonight. 23:40. North fence.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: You're going in there. (It isn't a question.) Then take these.
A heavy flashlight and a pair of bolt cutters.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Not the shotgun. You'd shoot your own foot.
Merrow Paper Mill. Brick sheds, a smokestack, broken windows. But warm light leaks from the pulping hall, and steam rises from the boiler house. A sign: CLOSED 2009. PRIVATE PROPERTY.
23:40. The camera on the fence post stops blinking. Twelve minutes.
You cut the fence. Ahead, the yard: a gravel path straight to the pulping hall, or the long way round through the dead grass.

choices.label: Through the grass, the long way

fx.toast: Gravel crunches. A guard looks your way.

lines.text: A guard's flashlight swings along the wall toward you. Behind you, a stack of pallets. To your left, an open shed door.

The paper machines are gone. In their place: plastic sheeting, ventilation fans, a long steel table. Three workers in respirators feed powder into two pill presses that thump out small blue tablets stamped M30.
Counterfeit oxycodone. Which means fentanyl.
Blue barrels of chemical sludge stand by the loading door, waiting.

puzzle.title: The lab
puzzle.prompt: Photograph everything. Quietly.

spots.text: Two industrial presses. Thump. Thump. Thump. A tray of blue tablets fills every few seconds.
Blue plastic barrels with hazard labels peeled off. One is cracked; something milky has dried down its side. The smell makes your eyes water.
Batch numbers, dates, and counts in the thousands. At the bottom: "BOAT — TUE/FRI".
Respirators, gloves, hairnets. One of them is barely older than Tess.

lines.text: A sealed bag of pills sits on the end of the table, a metre from the nearest worker's back. Physical evidence. If you can reach it.

choices.label: Crouch-walk out and grab the bag
Leave it. The photos are enough.

lines.text: You crouch. The worker shifts his weight. The press thumps.

choices.label: Wait for him to turn away

lines.text: Your hand closes on the bag between one thump and the next. You're back in the shadows before the press lands again.
The worker turns. Your eyes meet over his respirator. He opens his mouth. You run, and he hesitates just long enough. You don't get the bag.
Heat hits like a wall. Humid, green, almost beautiful. Rows of glass tanks under heat lamps.

Tiny poison dart frogs, bright blue and yellow. Radiated tortoises from Madagascar stacked in crates. Slow lorises in small cages, blinking. And at the far end, a locked glass vault with a brass plate: B. INSULARIS — ILHA DA QUEIMADA GRANDE — 6.
Only five snakes inside. The one from Eli's bucket came from here. Someone took it back.
You step back and your shoulder catches a heat-lamp cable. The lights flicker, buzz, and die. In the dark, somewhere close, a tank latch clicks.
Your flashlight finds it: gold coils on the floor, a metre in front of your boots, head lifting.
It slides past your boot. It's behind you now, between you and the door. A pipe runs along the floor to your right.

choices.label: Step over the pipe, away from it
Turn and shine the light on it

lines.text: It rises. Its head sways at knee height, tasting the heat of you.
You back out of the boiler house one slow step at a time. The snake loses interest and coils under a tank.
Behind you, a worker swears in the dark: "Which idiot left the lamp off?"
The old mill manager's office, upstairs. A keypad on the door. Beside it, a framed Diwali card, of all things, signed "V.K. — every lock should remember the day it all began."
Next to it, a framed newspaper clipping: "KESSLER RESTRUCTURING TAKES OVER MERROW MILL HOLDINGS — signed March 14, 2019."
Four digits.

puzzle.title: The keypad
puzzle.prompt: The day it all began. Four digits.
hints: Month and day, two digits each.

lines.text: Leather chairs, whisky, a hotel-suite carpet. On the desk, a large glass terrarium with one golden lancehead, bigger than the rest. A brass tag: MIDAS.
Victor's laptop is open. A spreadsheet.

puzzle.title: Victor's laptop
puzzle.prompt: Ninety seconds before it locks. Copy everything to your USB stick.

spots.text: D.C. — "law": $4,000/month. G.P. — runs: $1,200 per run. B.H. — sponsorship: $30,000 per year. Venom, 6 × B.I.: $210,000. And at the bottom: H. — 60%. D.C. is Dale Corbin. G.P., Gus Pell. B.H., Brian Holt. H…?
One file: Hades_contacts.enc. Encrypted. You copy it anyway.
An email from a blocked sender: "Clean before Friday. Don't make me come down there. — H"

lines.text: Footsteps on the stairs. You duck behind the terrarium. Victor comes in with Corbin, mid-conversation.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: …and I don't care what he looks like, Dale. He's a nice boy from Windsor with a box of sweets. Nice boys go home if you ask them correctly.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: And the sister?

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Hades wants her found before she broadcasts again. She knows his voice. Nobody knows his voice.
He taps the terrarium. Midas rises.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Find her, Dale. Or I find a use for you.
Corbin leaves. Victor pours a whisky and talks to the snake.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Festival of lights, Midas. Good triumphs over evil. (He laughs.) Every year, they still believe it.
An alarm whoops. The camera reset is over. A guard with a shotgun sees you at the office window.

lines.speaker: GUARD
lines.text: HEY!
The window beside your head explodes. You run.
Down from the office: a catwalk across the hall, or the stairs to the yard.
Two men ahead. Cover: a row of barrels, or a parked truck.
A conveyor belt blocks the way. Over it or under it?
The fence, ten metres. Or the outflow ditch beside it.

choices.label: The gap in the fence you cut

lines.text: You're through the fence and into the trees before the first guard reaches the yard. Flashlights sweep the woods behind you, too late.
You lie in a ditch of freezing water, heart hammering, the USB stick clenched in your fist. A refrigerated truck rumbles past: MERROW PALLETS & SUPPLY. The cab light flicks on.
The driver is Gus Pell, still in his diner apron, humming.
Your phone buzzes. Unknown number. You answer and say nothing.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: You left your coffee cup at my truck stop, Mani. And your footprints all over my boiler house.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: You've got her eyes. Did anyone tell you that? Same stubborn eyes.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Here's my last offer. Go home. Light your lamps. Call your mother. Or I start taking the people you've met here. One at a time. Until you do.
The line goes dead. On the hill, the red light on the water tower blinks twice.
End of Episode 4.
You wake on the couch. Your palms are torn from the fence wire and one cut on your hand won't stop bleeding through the tissue.
Tess, getting ready for her shift, sees the blood on the cushion and drops her mug.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: That needs stitches. We're going to Dr. Rao. Now.

choices.label: Tell Tess the truth about the mill

lines.text: A small clinic with faded flu-shot posters. Dr. Anika Rao, forty-six, sharp, exhausted, examines you with gloved hands.

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: Four stitches. Wire, not glass. (beat) There's only one fence in this town with wire like that. You've been up at the mill.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: There's a lab up there. And a room full of animals. Golden lanceheads, from Brazil.
She stops wrapping the bandage.

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: I don't know anything about that. Keep it clean. Come back if it blackens.
She's already turning away. You have one chance to make her listen.

choices.label: Show her the 46 callers on the map
"My sister is missing because of this."

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: (very quietly) I have that map. I drew it myself in 2015. Nobody wanted it.
She folds her arms.

choices.label: Show her the photos of the blue M30 pills
Show her the bag of pills

lines.text: Dr. Rao goes white.

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: Four overdoses since spring. Young people. I was told to sign them as heart failure.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Told by whom?

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: The county coroner. Who is also our sheriff.
She turns her back to you, very deliberately, and puts a small brass key on the counter beside the sink.

lines.speaker: DR. RAO
lines.text: I go to lunch at one. The back door sticks. Everyone knows that.

Wood panelling, burnt coffee, a wall of framed photos. Corbin with the mayor. Corbin at a fish fry. Corbin shaking hands at a ribbon cutting, captioned "Mill Holdings partners, 2019". Victor, younger, smiling in the background.
At a side desk, a young deputy types slowly, watching everything. His name plate says S. ORTIZ.
You're here to file a missing persons report. Corbin takes it personally.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Your sister had a gift for stirring things up. People here don't like being stirred.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: When did you last speak to her?

choices.label: "Sunday night. She left me a voicemail."

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: And what have you been doing in town all week?

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: (writing nothing down) Anything else? Anything you've seen?

choices.label: "Trucks on the mill road at two in the morning."

lines.text: Corbin relaxes, almost bored with you.
His radio squawks. He steps into the back room. His desk drawer is open about an inch.
A thick envelope of cash, rubber-banded, with a sticky note: "Nov — V." Under it, a folder: Coroner's reports — Greyhaven, 2026. Four death certificates, all signed "cardiac arrest".
Three seconds. Three photos. You're back in your chair when Corbin comes out.
You stay put. Corbin comes back, hands you a form, and watches you fill it in. Across the room, Deputy Ortiz is watching too. Watching the drawer.
Ortiz walks you to your car. Out of Corbin's earshot, he speaks without turning his head.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: Did your sister ever say my name?

choices.label: "No. But she said someone at the station was decent."

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: I didn't sign up to be anybody's dog. (beat) Two of those kids who died, I went to school with their brothers.
He glances at the station.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: The men at that mill carry rifles, Mani. You don't.
He opens his trunk and hands you a small revolver wrapped in a cloth.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: Confiscated off a poacher last year. It's not in any system. I didn't give you this.
Behind the old gravel pit, Ortiz sets three cans on a log.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: Six rounds. Every one counts. Show me how you'd do it.

puzzle.title: First lesson
puzzle.prompt: Put the steps in the order Ortiz teaches them.
items: Check it's loaded and point it downrange
Line up the sights on the target
hints: Sights before breath, breath before trigger.
puzzle.answerText: Safety, grip, stance, sights, breath, squeeze.

lines.text: You miss the first can. You miss the second. The third jumps off the log. The sound is enormous. Your ears ring and your hands shake.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: I write code, man.

lines.speaker: ORTIZ
lines.text: Then think of it as the last line. You hope you never reach it.
Gus is smoking by the dumpsters. You step out of the shadow behind him and hold up your phone: the ledger. "G.P. — runs, $1,200 per run."
Gus drops the cigarette.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: The diner's been losing money for nine years. My wife's chemo wasn't covered. Victor came in with an envelope.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: I drive. That's all. I don't look in the back.

choices.label: "Then you'll talk to the police. Today."
"Help me, and I'll tell them you did."

lines.text: Gus panics. He talks fast, too fast, to make you go away.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Saturday. Tomorrow night. The last run. Victor's shutting it all down. The lab, the animals, everything into the lake. Then he burns the mill.
He goes back inside. Through the window, you see him pick up the phone.
Gus looks at you for a long time. Then he sits down on an upturned milk crate.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: Saturday night. Tomorrow. The last run. Victor's shutting it all down: the lab, the animals, everything into the lake. Then he burns the mill for the insurance. He wants it clean before the partner comes to look.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Hades.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: I've never seen him. Nobody has. Victor calls him Mark when he's drunk. Just Mark.

lines.speaker: GUS
lines.text: If you need a truck, or a road, or a door left open, you call me.
The back door sticks, exactly as promised. A narrow room of filing cabinets and boxes going back to 1979. Thirty years of a town's bodies, on paper.
You do what you know. You treat it like a dataset.

puzzle.title: Sort by street
puzzle.prompt: Lung illness, rashes, rare cancers. Where do the addresses cluster?

options.t: The new subdivision by the highway

options.why: Not even close. Look at the street column.

lines.text: Now the four 2026 "cardiac" deaths. You line up their dates against Ruth's truck log.

puzzle.title: Sort by date
puzzle.prompt: Each of the four deaths happened…

options.t: …within two days after a Tuesday or Friday night boat

lines.text: Clipped to the last file, in Dr. Rao's handwriting: "Not cardiac. Fentanyl. Signed under protest. A.R."
You photograph everything. Thirty years. Four kids. One road.
Dusk. The motel sign is dark. The office door is open.
Inside: drawers on the floor. The stuffed pike smashed. Ruth's scanner stamped flat on the tiles, still hissing. Her chair tipped over. The shotgun gone.
The floorboard behind the desk is still in place. You lift it. Fourteen notebooks, untouched. She hid them before they came.
On the counter, set neatly in the middle of the mess: Victor's business card. On the back, in the same neat hand as the note on the Marsh dock:
"One at a time."
Outside, your car sits on four slashed tyres. Out on the lake, the church bell rings six. Then, a seventh time. It never does that.
End of Episode 5.
You, Eli and Ortiz, off duty in a hoodie, have searched the lakeshore for Ruth for four hours. Her skiff is gone from its mooring. That's all you found.
Ortiz leaves to cover his night shift so Corbin won't suspect him. Eli falls asleep in a chair, boots still on.
Your phone lights up. Amma, video call. It's Saturday morning in Vellore. Behind her, oil lamps lined up on the windowsill. Appa is hanging a string of mango leaves over the door.

lines.speaker: AMMA
lines.text: Kanna! Naalaiku Deepavali. Nila-va kooppidu, rendu pasangalaiyum onna paakkanum.
lines.subtitle: Kanna! Tomorrow is Deepavali. Call Nila over, I want to see both my children together.

choices.label: "Amma, Nila-va kaanom. Naan thedittu irukken. Promise-aa kandupidipen."
choices.sub: Amma, Nila's missing. I'm searching for her. I promise I'll find her. (The truth.)

choices.label: "Ava kulichittu irukka, Amma, naalaiku call pannuva."
choices.sub: She's having a bath, Amma, she'll call you tomorrow. (Protect them.)

lines.text: Amma's face crumples. She puts her hand over her mouth. Appa takes the phone from her, and his voice is steady.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Appo kandupidi, kanna. Naanga vilakku yethi kaathirukkom.
lines.subtitle: Then find her, kanna. We'll light the lamps and wait.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Mani. Airport-la unna anuppa vandhappo nee sonna, "Naan avala paathukuren, Appa." Naan oru naalum sandhegapattadhilla.
lines.subtitle: Mani. When we came to see you off at the airport, you said, "I'll look after her, Appa." I have never doubted it.

lines.text: Amma beams. She tells you what she's cooking. She tells you to make Nila wear the green silk. You say yes to everything.

lines.speaker: APPA
lines.text: Mani. Airport-la unna anuppa vandhappo nee sonna, "Naan avala paathukuren, Appa." Naan oru naalum sandhegapattadhilla.
lines.subtitle: Mani. When we came to see you off at the airport, you said, "I'll look after her, Appa." I have never doubted it.

lines.text: The call ends. You sit alone in the dark flat with the lie, and it is very heavy.
A small stone church on the hill, lit by candles. The bell rope hangs in a corner. An old priest pulls it for seven o'clock, slowly, exactly seven times.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Last night it rang seven at six o'clock.

lines.speaker: FATHER REID
lines.text: It did. Ruth Vane and I have an arrangement, from years ago, when she first started writing down trucks. If anyone ever came for her, I was to ring once more than the hour.

lines.speaker: FATHER REID
lines.text: It means she got away. It means she's safe.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Where?

lines.speaker: FATHER REID
lines.text: She didn't tell me, so no one could make me tell them. But she left a message, if you came asking. (He reads from a folded paper.) "Get the camera from the church. It's what Nila went back for. Then the water will bring you to me."

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: This church?

lines.speaker: FATHER REID
lines.text: No, son. The other one. The one underneath the lake.
Rows of boxes. Parish records. Photographs of Old Merrow: a schoolhouse, a general store, a stone church with a tall spire, families in Sunday clothes.

lines.speaker: FATHER REID
lines.text: I was born down there. Baptised in that church. When they flooded the valley, they promised us the water would be clean. They moved our dead up the hill. (beat) Not all of them.

puzzle.title: The archive
puzzle.prompt: Look through the boxes.

spots.text: A photo: mill trucks parked beside the old church before the flood. Young men rolling barrels down the slope. One of them, unmistakably, is a nineteen-year-old Walter Marsh.
A plan of the old church: main doors at the west, a side door at the north into the bell tower, a crypt beneath the altar. Useful, if you were ever inside it underwater.

The dam opening: a crowd, a ribbon, officials in hard hats. The caption: "R. Hayden, Merrow Dam Authority, opens the gates." At the edge of the crowd, a figure in a long dark coat, face turned away. The same coat. The same posture. Forty-eight years ago.
Baptisms, weddings, funerals, 1842 to 1978. The last entry, in a shaking hand: "The bell is moved to the new church. Let it ring for those below."

lines.text: You show Walter the 1977 photo. He looks at it for a long time.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: Fifty dollars a night. I bought Margaret's ring with it. I've been paying for that ring my whole life.

lines.speaker: WALTER
lines.text: I told Father Tom, in confession, forty years ago. He never told a soul. (He stands.) My old diving gear's in the shed. The hose is good. I'll run the compressor myself. Eli steers.

choices.label: "You were nineteen. Help me now and it counts."
"You let this whole town get sick."

lines.text: Walter's old aluminium workboat. A small petrol compressor chugging on deck. A long yellow air hose. The fog is lifting into a grey, cold day.
You're in Walter's ancient wetsuit, a mask, a waterproof flashlight, Nila's map sealed in a plastic sleeve on your wrist. Your phone in a waterproof pouch.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Three tugs on the line means pull you up. You tug three times, we pull. Don't be a hero.
You roll backward off the side.
Green darkness. Then shapes. A drowned village, perfectly still.
Your breath roars in your ears. The yellow hose trails up behind you to a pale disc of light.

puzzle.title: Old Merrow
puzzle.prompt: Swim down the main street toward the church. Photograph what you find.

spots.text: A chalkboard still on the wall. Rows of rotted desks. A child's tin lunchbox on the floor, rusted shut.
A faded sign: MERROW GENERAL — EST. 1891. A shelf of jars, still sealed, full of something dark.
Headstones leaning in the silt. Some graves were never moved. "Reid, Thomas and Agnes." Father Reid's grandparents.

The ground changes. Rusted 1977 barrels half-buried in silt. On top of them, dozens of newer blue barrels, some split open, leaking a slow milky cloud. Dead fish, belly up in the weeds. A sunken wire cage holding the shells of dead tortoises: animals that didn't survive the trip, dumped like rubbish. You photograph all of it.

lines.text: You swim through the open doors of the church. Pews in rows. A fallen cross. A stained-glass window glowing faintly green. Barrels stacked to the rafters down the aisles.
In the front pew, wedged under the kneeler, where she must have dropped it when her own air ran low: a yellow dive-camera housing. NILA, in marker on the strap.
You pull it free. A barrel shifts above you. Then another. A slow avalanche of steel. Silt explodes into the water and the light goes brown.
Brown nothing. Your flashlight shows only your own hand. Then, faintly: clank. Clank. Clank. Walter, tapping a wrench on the hull above. Louder to your left.
You try to remember which way you came in.

choices.label: Follow the tapping, left along the wall
Back the way you came, toward the main doors

lines.text: Barrels. A wall of barrels where the doors were. The avalanche has blocked the main entrance. You turn back.
The tapping, to your left.
Your hand finds stone steps going down. The crypt. Absolutely not. You turn around, heart slamming.
The tapping, to your left.
Your glove finds a wooden door frame. A narrow doorway. Above it, the silt is thinner, and there's grey light.

choices.label: Swim up through the bell tower

lines.text: The wall goes on. The tapping is directly above the doorway you just passed. You go back.
You rise through the drowned bell tower. Daylight above, a pale disc. The shadow of Walter's boat. And beside it, a second hull: longer, darker, an outboard idling.
You draw a breath from the regulator. Air comes. Then half a breath. Then nothing.
You look up. The yellow air hose drifts down past your face, cut clean. On the surface, a gloved hand pulls back into the second boat. A blade flashes.
You tug three times on the hose. It comes down limp into your hands.
Four metres to the surface. Your lungs burn. The light gets further away.
End of Episode 6.
Black. A muffled boom through the water: a shotgun. Then a hand grabs your harness and hauls you upward. Eli, who dived in after you without a mask.

You break the surface choking. A small skiff roars out of the fog. Standing in it, soaked, grey hair loose, shotgun at her shoulder: Ruth Vane. She fires again over the second boat. Its outboard screams and it flees into the fog.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Told you I sleep light.
Walter, shaking, wraps you in a blanket. You check the yellow housing in your arms. Nila's camera is safe.
Ruth steers north toward a dark wooded headland. An old steel radio tower rises out of the trees. Pike Point.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: They came Thursday night. Two of them. I went out the back with Harold's shotgun and took the skiff. I've been at Jonah Pike's cabin since.

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: Nila told me once: "If I'm not home, I'm with Jonah." Jonah won't tell even me where she is. Stubborn old goat.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Is she—

lines.speaker: RUTH
lines.text: He says she's alive. He says it every day. I choose to believe him.

A log cabin crammed with radios: shortwave sets, oscilloscopes, a wall of QSL cards from around the world. Jonah Pike, seventy, white beard, a cardigan full of holes, looks at you over his glasses for a long time.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: You're Anna. She talks about you on the air when she thinks nobody's listening. (beat) Somebody always was.
He's recorded every one of Nila's 23:00 broadcasts. And something else.

puzzle.title: Jonah's tapes
puzzle.prompt: Listen to the recordings.

spots.text: Nila broadcasting about the callers. Then, on a frequency right beside hers, a man's calm voice: "Brave girl."
Nila describing the night boats. The voice again: "You're very close now, Nila."

The voice from your car radio: "He's already here." And then, on a private channel Jonah caught by luck, the same voice speaking to someone else: "Victor, you're sloppy. Clean it before I come. Or I clean you."
"Uses relays. Bounces off three or four repeaters. Can't fix his position. A professional. Victor is afraid of him. You can hear it."

lines.text: You connect Nila's camera to Jonah's monitor. Timestamped last Sunday, 22:10.
Underwater: the barrels, the dead tortoises, a milky cloud. Then Nila surfaces under a dock and films the boat above it. Victor and Corbin, side by side, watching workers drop a crate over the side.

lines.speaker: CORBIN
lines.text: Is that the last of the dead ones?

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: The ones Hades won't pay for, yes.
The camera turns to Nila's face, lit by her dive torch, whispering:

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: If someone's watching this, I didn't make it back. Barrels at St. Brendan's. Victor Kessler. Sheriff Corbin. Tell everyone.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: She made it back. (To Jonah.) Take me to her.
Jonah leads you and Ruth up a rough path through the pines. Wind off the lake. Above, the rusted tower, a single red aircraft light still blinking at the top.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: That was 94.1's original transmitter, till they moved it into town in '98. They left everything. I kept it alive, out of spite. (beat) It still reaches every radio in the county.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: That's how she broadcast on 94.1 when the station was off.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: Watch your feet. She's rigged the trail. Trip wires, tin cans, a flare.
Your flashlight catches a glint at ankle height between two pines. Or was it just ice?

choices.label: Brush it aside with your boot

fx.toast: Tin cans rattle in the trees.

lines.text: A fallen log across the path. The obvious step is right in the middle.

fx.toast: Cans clatter. Somewhere a bird explodes from a tree.

choices.label: Climb over at the root end

lines.text: The shed is in sight. A string of fishing line runs low across the last metre, tied to a flare stake.

choices.label: Duck under at the stake end, where it's highest

lines.text: You reach the shed without a sound. Jonah nods, impressed.

A concrete shed at the foot of the tower. A camp stove, a sleeping bag, tins of beans, a crate of bottled spring water (half empty), a rack of humming transmitter equipment. Nila's radio bag on a hook.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Stop right there.
She steps from behind the transmitter rack with a flare gun in a shaking hand. Thinner. Hair tied back. A scrape across one cheek.
She sees your face. The flare gun drops.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Anna?
For a long moment, neither of you moves. Then she's across the shed and you're holding her, and she's crying and laughing and hitting your shoulder.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Naan dhaan vara vendaamnu sonnene!
lines.subtitle: I told you not to come!

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Eppo naan un pechu kettirukken?
lines.subtitle: Since when do I listen to you?

lines.text: Ruth and Jonah step outside to give you a minute. You sit on the sleeping bag together.
There's so much to say. Where do you start?

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Amma-ku theriyuma?
lines.subtitle: Does Amma know?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Illa. Nee kulichittu irukkannu sonnen.
lines.subtitle: No. I told her you were having a bath.

lines.text: Nila laughs, then stops laughing.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Naalaiku naane solren.
lines.subtitle: I'll tell her myself tomorrow.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Corbin's car outside the flat. Men on the stairs. I went out the back with my radio bag, along the shore in the dark, all the way to Jonah's.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Phone-a vittutu odinen. Rangoli-a paadhi-la vittutten. Kaalaila thirumbi varuvennu nenachen.
lines.subtitle: I ran and left my phone. I left my rangoli half done. I thought I'd be back by morning.

lines.text: Nila goes quiet.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Avan enakku badhil sonnaan. Ovvoru raathiriyum. Naan enna dress pottirukkennu avanukku theriyum. Naan azhudhadhu kooda theriyum. Water tower-ai vida pakkathula naan avana paathadhe illa.
lines.subtitle: He answered me. Every night. He knew what I was wearing. He even knew when I cried. I never saw him closer than the water tower.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Naan night-la veliya poradha avan Corbin kitta sonnaan. Enakku theriyum. Avan mela kovapadaadha. Corbin Tess vaazhkaiya azhichiruppaan.
lines.subtitle: He told Corbin I went out at night. I know. Don't be angry with him. Corbin would have destroyed Tess's life.

lines.text: You pull a gift-wrapped box out of your soaked duffel. The bow is crushed.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Happy Deepavali. Oru naal munnaadiye.
lines.subtitle: Happy Deepavali. A day early.

lines.text: She unwraps it. A new handheld ham radio. She laughs through tears.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Oru crime scene vazhiya naalu mani neram drive panni enakku radio kondu vandhiya?
lines.subtitle: You drove four hours through a crime scene to bring me a radio?

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Sweets-um dhaan. Konjam nanaanjiduchu.
lines.subtitle: And sweets. They got a bit wet.

lines.text: The four of you around the camp stove, the proof spread on the concrete floor.
Jonah nudges the crate of water bottles with his boot.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: Where'd these come from? I never brought you water.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: They were here when I came. I thought you left them.
Jonah frowns. Then the plan takes over, and nobody mentions it again.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: There's no cell signal on Pike Point. If we drive out to call the police, Corbin's on every road. If we call 911 from town, it routes through Corbin's dispatch.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: So you don't call. You broadcast.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: At 23:00. On 94.1, to every radio in the county. On 7.185 for the ham operators. And Jonah patches it onto the provincial police band. (beat) They can bury a phone call. They can't bury a whole town hearing it.
The transmitter powers on. But the feed line up the tower is dead. A length of coax is missing.

choices.label: Use Nila's cut cable from the flat

fx.toast: The spare works, but the signal will be weaker.

lines.text: You climb to the first platform with the cable over your shoulder. Nila talks you through it on her new radio. You fit the coax. Now the dish has to face the town.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Turn it slowly. Watch the meter. Greyhaven's somewhere south-southwest.

puzzle.title: Align the antenna
puzzle.prompt: Turn the dish until the signal meter peaks.

lines.text: The signal meter glows green. Forty minutes to 23:00.
Eli arrives up the trail, out of breath, carrying a rifle from his father's closet.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Tess is safe. She's with Father Tom at the church. I came to help.
Nila hugs him. You don't.
Ten minutes later you step outside to check the trip wires and hear Eli around the side of the shed, low, into a handheld radio.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: …Pike Point. Now. (beat) I'm sorry.
You round the corner. Eli turns, guilty, the radio still in his hand.
Across the lake, an orange glow rises over the trees: the mill is burning. On the lake road below Pike Point, a line of headlights stops at the foot of the trail.
The new radio on Nila's belt crackles. A man's voice, warm, amused.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Nila. Mani. And Ruth, I assume, with Harold's shotgun. (beat) Let's talk about this like adults.
End of Episode 7.
You grab Eli by the collar and slam him against the shed wall.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Who was that?

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: Ortiz! It was Ortiz! (He holds up the radio. The channel tag reads GPS-2, the deputy's private channel.) I told him to come to Pike Point with everyone he trusts.

lines.speaker: ELI
lines.text: I said sorry because… because I'm the reason they knew where Nila slept. I've been saying sorry to everyone all week.

choices.label: Take the rifle away from him

lines.text: Nila looks down at the headlights on the lake road.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Then who brought them?

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: Victor has a man on that water tower who sees everything. He's been watching this headland for days.

e8_offer.place: Pike Point trail, below the tower

lines.text: Victor walks up the trail alone, a flashlight in one hand, both hands visible, his coat immaculate even in the mud. Below him, four men with rifles spread into the trees. Corbin stays by the cars.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Mani! I brought no snakes, I promise.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Let's be practical. The mill's gone. Burned tonight, very sad, old wiring. There's no lab, no animals, no evidence. Just a camera, some photographs, and a very tired young woman.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Two hundred thousand dollars. Enough to bring your parents over. Enough to never write another job application.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: No? Then something you can't buy. Corbin's video of the Marsh girl at the till goes away forever. Eli's family keeps the dock. Everyone goes home.
Victor's smile thins.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: I'm not the one you should be afraid of, Mani. My partner doesn't negotiate. If you broadcast, he'll come to Windsor himself. To your little apartment. To your parents' shop in Ranipet.
You hear yourself say yes. Victor smiles, warm as a fireplace. Behind you, Nila makes a sound you will hear for the rest of your life.
By morning the transmitter is smashed, the camera is at the bottom of the lake, and Nila won't look at you.
No. Not like this. Try again.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: You know what my father said to me when I left India? "Look after her." That's the whole job, Victor. That's all I came here to do.
Victor's smile is gone.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Then you'll do it in the dark.
He raises a hand. The floodlights on the trucks below snap on.
You have the revolver: six rounds. Ruth has the shotgun. Jonah has a flare gun. Eli is locked in the shed with Nila. Nila is inside warming up the transmitter for 23:00.
Wave one: two men moving up through the pines toward the tree line.

choices.label: Let Ruth's shotgun pin them; hold your fire
Empty the revolver into the trees

lines.text: Ruth fires twice. Bark explodes beside the first man and both of them drop flat behind a log.
You fire once, carefully, when one of them raises his head. You miss. He stays down. Five rounds left.
You fire three times into the dark. Two shots hit trees. The third hits a man in the leg and he goes down screaming. A rifle round sparks off the shed doorframe beside your head.
Three rounds left. Your hands won't stop shaking.
Wave two: a man behind the shed with bolt cutters at the transmitter's power cable. At the same moment, a rifle round hits the doorframe and Jonah goes down, splinters in his arm.
You round the shed. The man has the bolt cutters on the cable. You shout. He turns, and you fire. He drops the cutters and runs into the trees, holding his shoulder.
Ruth is already kneeling beside Jonah, tying her scarf around his arm. He swears at her inventively. He'll live.
You drag Jonah behind the doorframe. Behind the shed, a heavy clunk. The lights inside flicker. Nila shouts.
You get there in time to see the man running, the cable half cut. Nila splices it with tape and swearing. It holds. Barely.
Wave three: a man is climbing the tower ladder to cut the antenna feed. You go up after him.
On the first platform, wind howling, he swings a wrench at your head.

choices.label: Duck and drive your shoulder into him

lines.text: The wrench whistles over your head. You hit him low. He goes over the rail and crashes into the bushes below, groaning. Alive.
The wrench catches your forearm and the revolver nearly goes over the edge. You hold on to it. You hit him with your whole body and he goes over the rail into the bushes below. Your arm screams.
No sirens come. Corbin stays by the cars, smoking, waiting. Victor's men pull back into the trees to regroup.
Ruth reloads with steady hands. "They'll come again," she says. "Do your thing, girl. Fast."
You check the revolver. One round left.
The signal meter glows green, but only just. Jonah's spare cable is short and the needle trembles. Nila pulls on her headphones. Her hands are steady now.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: Good evening, Greyhaven. This is After Hours on 94.1. I'm Nila. I'm back. (beat) And tonight I'm going to tell you everything.
She looks at you. You have to hand her the proof in an order a listener, and a police officer, can follow.

puzzle.title: The broadcast
puzzle.prompt: Put the proof in order: from what the town suffered, to the cause, to who did it.
items: The callers' map: what the town has been suffering
Dr. Rao's records: the illness, and four "cardiac" deaths that were fentanyl
The lab photos: where the fentanyl comes from
The Old Merrow photos: where the waste goes
Nila's footage: Victor and Corbin, on camera, together
hints: Start with the people: the callers, then the medical records.
Then the cause (lab, dumping). The ledger and the footage name names, so they come last.

lines.text: Halfway through the ledger, the signal meter crashes to red. Nila's headphones fill with her own voice, slowed down, a few seconds behind, distorted.

lines.speaker: JAMMING VOICE
lines.text: …If anyone's on seven-one-eight-five… I found it… aana andha—
lines.subtitle: …If anyone's on seven-one-eight-five… I found it… but don't trust the—

lines.text: Her private voicemail to you. Only someone tapping her phone could have that.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: (clutching his bleeding arm, squinting at a scope) Somebody's flooding 94.1 from the north. The water tower. Big transmitter. That's not Victor's gear.

lines.speaker: JONAH
lines.text: Ruth. Your notebooks. Fourteen years of scanner channels. Find me one the provincial police listen to overnight, that he isn't covering.

puzzle.title: Beat the jamming
puzzle.prompt: Ruth reads from her 2019 notebook: "OPP overnight dispatch, northern relay: one-five-five point four-six." Tune the transmitter to it.
hints: Slide slowly near 155.5 and watch the meter.
puzzle.answerText: The jamming wins. The broadcast dies.

lines.text: The meter climbs back to green on the new channel. Nila finishes it all: the ledger, the footage, her own whisper from the bottom of the lake. She ends it the way she ended every show.

lines.speaker: NILA
lines.text: This was After Hours. Lock your doors, Greyhaven. And thank you for listening.
Nila steps outside for air. A hand clamps over her mouth. Victor, mud on his coat now, a pistol in his hand, drags her up the tower ladder to the first platform.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: MANI!
You climb. On the platform, wind howling, Victor holds Nila at the rail with the pistol to her head. You raise the revolver. One round. Your hands shake.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: One bullet. I counted. (He laughs, breathing hard.) You're not a killer, Mani. You're a nice boy with a spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: MANI
lines.text: Let her go. It's over.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: Over? You think I'm the top? I'm middle management. You think he'll let me sit in a courtroom?
He looks north, toward the water tower, and for the first time, he looks afraid.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: He's listening right now. He's always listening. His name is—
A single rifle crack across the water from the north.
Victor jerks. He looks down at his chest, surprised. The pistol slips from his fingers.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: …Hades doesn't… leave…
He falls. Thirty metres into the dark pines.
Nila crumples into your arms. You're still holding the revolver. You never fired. On the water tower across the lake, a tiny red light blinks twice and goes dark.
Headlights at the foot of the trail. Corbin's cruiser. In the back seat, a pale face against the glass. Tess.
Victor's voice on the radio, very calm.

lines.speaker: VICTOR
lines.text: The Marsh girl for the little USB stick in your pocket, Mani. The encrypted one. Bring it down. Alone.
You never promised to protect her. Nobody was watching her. You walk down the trail with the USB in your hand.
